name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog: Two fixes prompted by a friend's real setup attempt today. (1) Federation only ever talked to a remote's stock Jellyfin API (Items, Users, PlaybackInfo, ...), so nothing about a normal sync actually proved the remote was running Federation itself - it would keep pulling from any reachable Jellyfin server forever, even after Federation was uninstalled there. Every sync now probes the remote's Plugins/Federation/Config route (registered only by this plugin, no API key needed) before pulling its libraries; if a remote no longer answers it, that server's items are actively removed (not just left stale) and nothing new is pulled from it until it reappears - the same removal path DeleteServer already used. (2) The config page's 'Test Server' connection check could report the unhelpful 'Connected but failed to get system info' with no way to tell why: /System/Info/Public (used to confirm reachability) needs no API key, but /System/Info (used right after, for the server name/version) does - so a bad, missing, or under-privileged key looked identical to a dead server. The message now says which: invalid/missing key, insufficient permissions, or the exact HTTP status returned.
